title: Vector indexes: exact search, ANN and filtered recall
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects vector indexes: exact search, ann and filtered recall with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The local lab includes exact vector search for transparent reference results and an optional real Qdrant backend.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Exact nearest-neighbor search scores every eligible vector. Approximate nearest-neighbor indexes trade some recall for lower latency and memory access. HNSW organizes a navigable graph; IVF partitions vectors into coarse cells and probes a subset. Index parameters affect recall, build cost and search latency.

Vector stores also manage IDs, payload metadata, persistence, updates and filters. FAISS focuses on vector indexing; Qdrant, Chroma, Weaviate, Pinecone and pgvector provide different deployment and database capabilities. Compare required filters, operations and durability before choosing.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Create a Qdrant collection with an explicit vector size and distance. Upsert stable point IDs with tenant, document version and permissions in payload. Query with the authenticated tenant filter and a top-k limit. Add payload indexes for frequent filters according to measured workload.

Measure ANN Recall@K against exact eligible search, not against all tenants. Tune graph/search effort or IVF probe count while plotting recall versus p95 latency. Small datasets may not benefit from approximation.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Filtering the top ten global neighbors after retrieval can return no authorized results even when relevant tenant documents exist. More seriously, passing the unfiltered context to generation leaks other tenants' evidence.

Test tenant isolation before ranking, deletion visibility, repeated upserts, incompatible dimensions and persistence across restart. Benchmark selective filters because their cost and recall can differ sharply from unfiltered search.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The local lab includes exact vector search for transparent reference results and an optional real Qdrant backend. Store backend type in the report; the exact baseline is not labeled a vector database deployment.
Release evidence should show recall, p95, memory, restart behavior and isolation invariants. A faster index with unauthorized context fails regardless of its similarity score.

title: Qdrant persistence and payload-filter integration tests
objectives: Qdrant persistence and payload-filter integration tests
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects qdrant persistence and payload-filter integration tests with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Retain a store smoke report containing mode, collection contract, point IDs, filtered query results and restart/deletion checks.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A vector database's operational behavior matters beyond nearest-neighbor arithmetic. Stable IDs make upserts replace the intended point, payloads provide tenant and source metadata, and persistence determines whether indexed evidence survives restart. A local in-memory index cannot demonstrate restart durability.

The Qdrant lab uses the real client in persistent local mode with explicitly synthetic three-coordinate vectors. This validates store mechanics and authorization filters without pretending the vectors came from a semantic model.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Create a collection with declared dimension and cosine distance, upsert alpha and beta points, then use query_points with a payload Filter requiring tenant=alpha. Close and reopen the client using the same path and repeat the query. Delete one point and assert it no longer appears.

For a server deployment, Compose supplies a persistent volume and service health checks. Local embedded mode and remote service mode have different concurrency and operational guarantees; label the mode in every artifact.
sections.code:
from qdrant_client import QdrantClient,models
client=QdrantClient(path='artifacts/qdrant')
flt=models.Filter(must=[models.FieldCondition(key='tenant',match=models.MatchValue(value='alpha'))])
# query_points uses the collection's declared metric
# result=client.query_points('fixtures',query=[1.,0.,0.],query_filter=flt,limit=3)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A test creates the collection in memory, closes it and falsely claims persistence. A client forgets the filter on a secondary retrieval path. Duplicate random IDs accumulate stale versions instead of replacing them.
Test repeated upserts, deletion, reopen, dimension mismatch and both positive/negative tenant queries. Verify the returned payload against the authenticated scope even after the database filter.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Retain a store smoke report containing mode, collection contract, point IDs, filtered query results and restart/deletion checks. ANN quality tests are separate and require a larger labeled corpus and an exact-search reference.

For SDETs, isolate database mechanics from embedding quality. A real persistent store over synthetic vectors is honest infrastructure evidence; a semantic retrieval claim additionally requires a trained encoder and relevant-document labels.
